name: Market Socialism
description: Publicly or collectively owned firms competing in a market, with overall planning and largely free prices.

name: State Capitalism
description: Markets and profit under state command, which plans, holds strategic sectors and coexists with private enterprise.

name: Developmentalism
description: Public investment and planning to industrialize the country, protecting domestic industry while it grows.

name: Social Liberalism
description: A market-based economy, with essential services guaranteed to all and rules that reduce inequality.

name: Pragmatism
description: No firm preference between public and private ownership, planning and markets, protection and openness: judges case by case.

name: Syndicalism
description: An economy organized by trade unions and workers' organizations, which run production and bargain for each sector.

name: Social Democracy
description: A market economy with a strong social safety net, broad public services and income redistribution.

name: Distributism
description: Property widely spread among families and small producers, rather than concentrated in large firms or a single center.

name: Liberalism
description: Private property and free competition as the base of the economy, with clear rules and limited intervention.

name: National Liberalism
description: A free market and a small state in the domestic economy, with openness abroad measured by the national interest.

name: Ordoliberalism
description: A free market within firm rules that protect competition and prevent monopolies.

name: Liberal Developmentalism
description: Markets and private initiative drive growth, with targeted public support for industry and infrastructure.

name: Corporatism
description: Economic sectors organized into corporations of employers and workers that negotiate and coordinate national production.

name: Austrian Liberalism
description: Free prices and individual choice, with strong private property and minimal interference in the economy.

name: Classical Liberalism
description: Free markets, private property and free trade, with the state focused on upholding laws, contracts and security.

name: Religious Traditionalism
description: Holds that faith and inherited traditions hold society together and should guide customs and laws.

name: Moderate
description: No firm lean between tradition and change in customs, nor between religion and secularism.

name: Progressivism
description: Supports change in customs and broader individual rights, with religion and public life kept separate.

name: Autocracy
description: Power concentrated in one person or group, without free elections or institutional limits.

name: Anarchism
description: Society organized without a central government, through voluntary agreements and self-management.

name: Minarchism
description: Public power reduced to the minimum: security, justice and defense, and nothing more.

name: Representative Democracy
description: Government chosen by free elections, with guaranteed rights and limits on power.

name: Council Communism
description: Decisions made by councils of workers and communities, elected from the bottom up.

name: Absolute Monarchy
description: A monarch with total, inherited power and no constitutional limits.

name: Technocracy
description: Decisions led by experts and technical knowledge rather than political contests.

name: Federalism
description: Power divided between a central government and self-governing regions.

name: Confederalism
description: Sovereign regions or peoples joined by a pact, with a weak center.

name: Municipalism
description: Strong decentralization: the most important political decisions rest with cities and local communities, which coordinate with one another.

name: Communalism
description: Local communities that govern themselves, with the economy and decisions held in common, without a central state.

name: Neocameralism
description: Territory run like a company, with a board answerable to shareholders.

name: Aristocracy
description: Rule by an elite chosen by birth, tradition or recognized merit.

name: Partocracy
description: Government by a single or dominant party that controls the state and society.

name: Theocracy
description: Government run by religious leaders or religious law.

name: Imperialism
description: Expanding the country's influence or control over other territories and peoples, by force and by politics.

name: Political Realism
description: Relations between countries are guided by interest and power, not by ideals.

name: Armed Neutrality
description: Staying out of other people's wars while keeping strong armed forces to defend one's own territory.

name: Pacifism
description: Rejects war and military force as a means, putting peace and negotiation first.

name: Internationalism
description: Cooperation among countries through shared institutions and agreements, with open trade.

name: Isolationism
description: Keeping the country out of foreign alliances and conflicts, focused on itself and with more closed borders.

name: Primitivism
description: Rejects industrial and modern technology, favoring a life close to nature and on a small scale.

name: Environmentalism
description: Accepts technology as long as it is limited by environmental protection.

name: Cosmopolitanism
description: Sees humanity as one community, with open borders and free movement of people.

name: Multiculturalism
description: Values several cultures living in the same country, each keeping its own traditions.

name: Ethnic Nationalism
description: The nation is defined by common origin and ancestry, and immigration should be tightly restricted.

name: Non-Interventionism
description: Not interfering in other countries' affairs, avoiding wars and involvements beyond one's own borders.

name: Direct Democracy
description: Important decisions made directly by citizens through plebiscites and referendums, with power decentralized.

name: Digital Democracy
description: Participation and decisions through digital means, with citizens voting and proposing directly on online platforms.

name: Pragmatic Liberalism
description: The market as the base of the economy, with practical rules and adjustments as circumstances require, and moderate trade openness.

name: Fascism
description: A strong state and a single party, with the nation above the individual and control over the economy and society.

name: Hypercentralism
description: All power concentrated in the central government, with no autonomy for regions or cities.

name: Centralism
description: A strong central government decides the essentials, with regions and cities subordinate to it.

name: Unitarism
description: A unitary state in which the center decides what matters most and delegates administration and some choices to regions and cities.

name: Regionalism
description: Autonomy for the regions, within a state that still keeps a common center.

name: Patchwork
description: A patchwork of sovereign cities and communities, largely privately run, each with its own rules.

name: Libertarianism
description: The state stays out of private life: few laws, little surveillance and broad individual freedom.

name: Social liberalism
description: Civil liberties protected by law, with the state guaranteeing rights and limiting abuses of power.

name: Legalism
description: Freedom and order within the law: rights guaranteed and rules enforced, with a state that is neither absent nor watchful.

name: Paternalism
description: The state protects and guides citizens, with economic support and defense of custom, even against their own choices.

name: Moralism
description: The law enforces customs and morals, usually religious in origin, and punishes what contradicts them.

name: Securitism
description: Security and order above all: more policing, surveillance and punishment, within institutions.

name: Regimentalism
description: A disciplined, hierarchical society with obedience, order and firm command, and little participation.

name: Totalism
description: The state controls every sphere of life, from the economy to private life, with no room for dissent.

name: Interventionism
description: Intervening abroad, politically or militarily, to defend the country's interests or values.

name: Globalism
description: Cooperation through global organizations such as the UN, with decisions and rules shared among countries.

name: Messianism
description: A religious or historical mission of the country, justifying the spread of its faith, values or destiny.

name: Colonialism
description: Occupying and governing overseas territories, settling them with colonists and treating local peoples as subordinates.

name: Nationalism
description: Priority to the interests and sovereignty of one's own nation, including in trade with other countries.

name: Civic nationalism
description: The nation is the community of citizens who share the same laws and institutions, whatever their origin.

name: Cultural nationalism
description: The nation is its culture, language and customs, which must be preserved and adopted by newcomers.

name: Religious nationalism
description: The nation's identity comes from its faith, and the state must defend and promote it.

name: Pan-Islamism
description: The Muslim community as a single nation, united by faith above the borders between countries.

name: Tribalism
description: Loyalty goes to the clan, the tribe or the community of origin, which comes before the state and the nation.

name: Individualism
description: The individual comes before the nation and the group, with autonomy and freedom to make their own choices.

name: Communitarianism
description: Values and bonds of local communities, such as family, neighborhood and tradition, give meaning to life in society.

name: Regional nationalism
description: The identity of the region, with its own language, history and autonomy, comes before the identity of the state.

name: Patriotism
description: Love of and loyalty to one's own country, its institutions and symbols, without an ethnic or religious basis.

name: Anti-colonial nationalism
description: The nation asserts itself against foreign rule: liberation, sovereignty and its own development.

name: Modernizing Nationalism
description: The nation asserts itself through modernization: a strong state, its own industry and technical advance, to match or surpass the great powers.

name: Proletarian internationalism
description: Class solidarity comes before the nation: what unites workers is labor and equality, not borders.

name: Workers' nationalism
description: The nation is the working class: a strong, centralized state serving workers, controlling the economy and leading society.

name: Agrarianism
description: Rural life and farming as the foundation of society, with the land in the hands of those who work it.

name: Techno-capitalism
description: Innovation and big technology companies drive progress, with free markets and little regulation.

name: Cyber-communism
description: Technology and automation serving a planned, common economy, with abundance for all.

name: Transhumanism
description: Overcoming the limits of the human body and mind with science and technology, such as life extension and merging with machines.

name: Neutrality
description: No strong position on technology and nature: weighs each case, neither rejecting nor celebrating technology.

name: Accelerationism
description: Accelerating technological progress and the changes it brings as much as possible, without brakes, as a path to transforming society.

name: National industrialism
description: Industry at the service of the nation: protecting national production and using state power to industrialize the country.

name: Capitalist industrialism
description: Industry and technical progress driven by private initiative and capital, with free markets.

name: Socialist industrialism
description: Industrialization and technical progress led by the state and public ownership, serving the collective.

name: Industrialism
description: Industry and technical progress as the engine of the country, combining state and private initiative as works best.

name: Modernism
description: Faith in technical and scientific progress as the engine of a fairer, more modern and rational society.

name: State socialism
description: The state owns and plans the whole economy, with central control of production, prices and trade.

name: Socialism
description: Social ownership of the means of production and economic equality, with planning and redistribution.

name: Social distributism
description: Property widely distributed among families and cooperatives, with a state that guarantees rights and social protection.

name: Market distributism
description: Property widely distributed among families and small producers, within a free, local market.

name: Mutualism
description: A free market with property in the hands of those who work: exchange among small producers and cooperatives, mutual credit and a small state.

name: Cameralism
description: The state manages the economy like a great household: public finances, promotion of production and an efficient bureaucracy.

name: Third way
description: A middle ground between capitalism and socialism: markets with social policies, without the extremes of either.

name: Keynesian liberalism
description: Free markets with the state acting to stabilize the economy and sustain employment and demand.

name: Feudalism
description: A local, hierarchical economy based on land and ties of service and protection between lords and peasants.

name: Internationalist socialism
description: A public, planned economy, with cooperation and open trade among peoples, above national borders.

name: Protectionism
description: Protectionist capitalism: private property and markets, with tariffs and barriers to protect national production.

name: Mercantilism
description: The state steers private enterprise to enrich the nation: export much and import little, with tariffs, monopolies and control of production.

name: Nationalism
description: The economy at the service of the nation: the state steers development, protects national production and prioritizes the country's interests.

name: Labourism
description: Work at the center of the economy: labor rights, strong unions and a state that protects workers.

name: Social progressivism
description: Cultural change with social justice: expanding rights and freedoms with redistribution and protection for the vulnerable.

name: Conservative liberalism
description: Free markets combined with traditional customs and values, with caution about social change.

name: Liberal conservatism
description: Preserving traditions within liberal institutions: gradual reform, guaranteed rights and limited government.

name: Progressive conservatism
description: Traditional values with social reform: the state supports families and the weak without breaking with custom.

name: Conservatism
description: Prudence and respect for tradition, family and institutions, with slow change and caution about immigration.

name: Traditionalist conservatism
description: Inherited customs, faith and community life matter more than material progress and modernization.

name: Reactionism
description: Reversing modern change and restoring the social order, customs and hierarchy of the past.

name: Paleoconservatism
description: Tradition, national sovereignty and restricted immigration, against interventionism and globalism.

name: Neoreaction
description: Critique of modern democracy and a return to hierarchy, combined with high technology and fragmented power.

name: Reactionary modernism
description: Technology and modernization at the service of a hierarchical, anti-liberal order with strong national identity.

name: Secularism
description: Reason, science and human rights as the basis of public life, with religion separated from the state.

name: Moderate atheism
description: Atheism without a crusade: no religious faith, no extreme stance on customs, and religion treated as a private matter.

name: Traditionalist atheism
description: No religious faith, yet attached to tradition, family and order as the basis of common life, without grounding them in God.

name: Secular conservatism
description: Tradition, order and national identity defended without a religious foundation.

name: Universalist traditionalism
description: Traditional faith and customs open to all peoples, welcoming those who come from outside.

name: Assimilationist progressivism
description: Progressive customs and a secular state, requiring newcomers to adopt the country's values.

name: Religious progressivism
description: Faith that inspires social justice, rights and welcome, and reform of customs.

name: Enlightenment
description: Reason, science, tolerance and progress against dogma and absolutism, with individual rights and liberties.

name: Objectivism
description: Reason and self-interest guide life, and only a free capitalism respects individual rights.

name: Nietzscheanism
description: Affirming life and creating one's own values, overcoming herd morality in favor of exceptional individuals.

name: Marxism
description: Culture, customs and institutions reflect power relations, and emancipating society requires transforming them along with the economy.

name: Stratocracy
description: Government run by the military, with the command of the armed forces holding state power.

name: Anarcho-monarchism
description: No modern state: free communities under the symbolic or voluntary authority of a king rooted in tradition.

name: Political Neutrality
description: Mixed positions, with no clear lean on who should govern or how much say the people should have.
